subject: Private deployment security intake — SOC2/HIPAA checklist & network diagram request
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@opshealth.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@opshealth.io>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy security intake — SOC2/HIPAA checklist & network diagram request

Hi Rachel / team,

Thanks for the demo earlier — that was helpful. As we move toward a procurement review, our security and compliance leads asked for a short intake so we can scope the Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment. Key asks from our side:

- Current SOC 2 posture (Type I/II, date, and scope)
- GDPR / HIPAA experience and controls (data residency, PHI handling)
- Typical KMS/HSM integrations and key separation model for private installs
- Network isolation options: VPC-only, dedicated physical air-gap, hybrid with data egress controls

I've attached our security intake (opshealth_security_rfi.pdf) — please confirm who on your side will fill it and provide a high-level network diagram showing where customer-managed nets, routers/firewalls, and KMS/HSM sit.

Can you also indicate feasibility of an air-gapped OVA package vs. a VPC appliance? Our security team wants a clear decision/risk matrix by EOD Friday so procurement can start finance approvals.

Appreciate a short reply with owners and ETA.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen
Head of InfoSec — OpsHealth
alice.jensen@opshealth.io

Attachment: opshealth_security_rfi.pdf (application/pdf, 245KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@opshealth.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy security intake — SOC2/HIPAA checklist & network diagram request

Hi Alice — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Quick summary from our side and proposed next steps below.

Summary of posture:
- SOC 2: Redwood has a scoped SOC 2 Type I for our Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated products; we are in progress for a Type II audit covering Private as a service target (control window opens Q3 2028, report expected Q4 2028). We can share SOC 2 Type I report and control mapping now; Type II evidence will be available after the audit window.
- HIPAA/GDPR: We routinely support HIPAA-covered workloads via BAAs and have documented GDPR processing and Data Subject Request procedures. For Private deployments, customers typically execute a BAA + deployment-specific data residency statements.
- KMS/HSM: Private deployments support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and optional HSM integration for key generation and wrapping. Keys at rest use customer KMS keys; we support envelope encryption and provide integration guides.

Network/isolation options and feasibility:
- VPC dedicated: standard option, customer customer-managed VPC peering or private endpoint into Redwood-managed control plane.
- Fully air-gapped: feasible as an on-prem package but involves more effort — our on-prem airgap build is a curated set of images and installer script; it will require a 2–3 week operations lead time plus qualification testing.
- Hybrid (controlled egress): common pattern where model weights remain in customer VPC and control plane has limited signed RPCs over specific ports — lower ops overhead than full air-gap.

Proposed owners & ETA:
- Karthik Iyer: will produce a one-page topology diagram (redwood-deploy-sample-diagram.png) showing the VPC and air-gap options — ETA: Wed, Jun 6 EOD.
- Monica Patel: will start the SOC 2 evidence pull and share existing Type I report and control mapping — ETA: Thu, Jun 7 COB.
- Rachel Kim (me): will populate answers to your RFI and share a link to our security questionnaire and integration guide — ETA: Thu, Jun 7 COB.

Next meeting? If that timeline works, let's book a 30-min follow-up on Friday to walk security through the diagram and remaining questions.

Attachments referenced: redwood-deploy-sample-diagram.png (preview attached)

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@opshealth.io>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy security intake — follow-ups & clarifications

Thanks Rachel — that looks like a good plan. A few clarifying questions from our infra/security architects:

1) For the air-gapped package: do you support an HSM-internal-only mode (FIPS-backed HSM) or is the integration limited to customer KMS endpoints? We need HSM-rooted keys for signing in our environment.

2) Evidence request: can you share the exact control IDs and mappings for data retention and logging (we'll add these to the RFI spreadsheet). If Type II isn't available yet, can you provide the list of controls you expect to be in scope?

3) Network diagram: please include the recommended firewall rules and a short list of ports/protocols for outgoing control traffic in the VPC scenario. Our network team prefers an explicit allowlist sample.

4) Timeline sensitivity: procurement has an internal date of Jun 22 for committed cost center approvals. If the full air-gapped delivery path requires 2–3 weeks operations plus qualification (per your note) — can Redwood commit to an accelerated path if we sign a statement of work today? What would that look like (additional fees for ops/validation)?

If you can reply inline to the attached RFI and share the diagram, we can move procurement forward this week.

Regards,
Alice

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@opshealth.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@opshealth.io>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy security intake — answers & next steps / action items

Alice — following up with the deliverables we discussed. Inline answers and attachments below.

1) Air-gap + HSM: we support both patterns. For highest assurance we recommend customer HSM (FIPS 140-2/3) integration where the HSM is in the customer environment and Redwood uses wrapped keys. For fully air-gapped packs we can provide an HSM-compatible configuration; if OpsHealth requires Redwood to manage a FIPS HSM on-prem we can discuss a managed-HSM add-on (recurring fee + procurement).

2) Controls & mappings: Monica has exported the Type I control list and our expected Type II scope; see link to the control mapping in the shared Drive (https://drive.google.com/opshealth/rfi-answers). We'll attach the Type I report separately via secure link within 24 hours.

3) Network diagram & firewall rules: attached is the sample diagram (redwood-deploy-sample-diagram.png). Key egress ports for the VPC control channel: 443 (TLS) to control.redwood-inference.com, 5222 (if messaging broker used — optional), 123 (NTP) — we recommend strict destination allowlist to specific IPs. We'll produce a one-page allowlist you can drop into firewall rules.

4) Accelerated ops path: we can commit to an expedited air-gap delivery if a SOW is signed within 48 hours. Typical ramp in that path: 10 business days for image build + 3 days for customer validation. Expedited ops incurs a one-time acceleration fee (estimate provided on request). Karthik will include the expedited timeline and a short decision matrix in the diagram deliverable.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Karthik Iyer — topology diagram + expedited path decision matrix (Wed Jun 6 EOD) — will upload to the shared Drive.
- Monica Patel — SOC 2 Type I report + control mapping (secure link) (Thu Jun 7 COB).
- Rachel Kim — completed RFI answers (shared Drive link) + 30-min follow-up invite for Fri Jun 8 10:00 AM PT (tentative).

If that schedule meets procurement's deadline (Jun 22), please confirm and we'll update the SOW template accordingly.

Best,
Rachel

Attachments: redwood-deploy-sample-diagram.png (image/png, 82KB)
